issues.description: Re-ingesting changed inputs only upserts and never removes stale results or aliases, so reports can include rows no longer present in the source tree.
NaN and infinity scores are accepted instead of rejected, causing NaN database crashes and infinity values to be clamped into valid-looking scores.
Format B assumes non-empty metrics is a dict; list, string, or number values raise AttributeError instead of producing a malformed_row warning.
Malformed XML raises ElementTree ParseError and crashes ingest instead of returning a structured warning.
Parsers load whole input files or XML trees into memory, making large or hostile inputs an easy denial-of-service risk.
Format A parses CSV one physical line at a time, so valid quoted CSV fields containing newlines are mishandled.
Format B relies on Python json.loads defaults, allowing non-standard NaN tokens that later break database writes.
Missing model, task, or run_id values are silently normalized to empty strings and inserted as valid records.
Duplicate run_id correction semantics are applied to every source, so duplicate CSV/XML records silently overwrite instead of warning.
The empty-directory error path still calls ingest first, creating or mutating the database before returning failure.
The SQLite schema lacks CHECK constraints for score range and non-empty required identifiers, so corrupted internal writes are not rejected defensively.
Tests validate generated fixtures well but miss negative coverage for malformed XML, non-finite numbers, unexpected JSON shapes, and stale-row reingest behavior.
